To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the genes that mediate breast metastasis to the human brain.
we isolated cells that preferential infiltrate the brain, and that these cells have unique molecular features that enable them to metastasize to the brain.
breast cancer cells can acquire specific functions to colonize different organs, and that the molecular mechanisms of metastasis to the lungs and the brain are distinct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that mediate breast tumour metastasis to the central nervous system, and with the elucidation of their molecular functions.
the mechanisms by which breast cancer cells metastasize to the brain and the identification of potential therapeutic targets.
the molecular basis for breast-cancer metastasis to the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain microenvironment, which is unique in its high content of endothelial cells, is the major driver of brain metastasis.
the molecular basis for metastasis to the central nervous system is largely unknown, and that the molecular basis is likely to be different for each patient.
the genes we have identified are not only mediators of metastasis to the CNS but are also mediators of metastases to the lung and liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is a special organ for metastasis, and we identified mediators of this metastatic step.

the metastatic process involves a series of molecular interactions that are mediated by a number of mediators, including COX2, HBEGF, EGFR and ST6GALNA5, that allow the cancer cells to extravasate through capillaries, to cross the blood–brain and to colonize the brain.
breast cancer metastases to the brain are mediated by specific mediators of extravascular migration, and by specific enhancers that enable the crossing of the blood–brain-barrier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast cancer metastases to the brain require a combination of factors that promote extravasation through the blood– brain barrier and that enhance brain colonization.
breast cancer brain metastasis involves the co-option of mediators of extravascular passage through the brain endothelial barrier.
breast cancer cells use distinct mechanisms to infiltrate different organs, and that the identification of these mediators may help to predict brain metastasis.
